documents.title: H&P - Admission - Septic Shock, Urinary Source
lines: ADMISSION H&P
Time of arrival ED 02:10. Admitted to ICU HD1 06:00.
CC: fever, chills, confusion x 1 day
HPI:
61 yo male brought in by son for 1 day of rigors, dysuria, flank pain and progressive lethargy.
Pt reports burning with urination x 4 days, urinary frequency, then shaking chills last evening.
Son notes pt was confused at home, would not answer questions appropriately, unsteady on feet.
No cough, no sputum, no chest pain, no diarrhea. Poor oral intake x 24h, no urine output noted since evening.
No recent instrumentation, no indwelling catheter, no recent hospitalization.
PMH: BPH, HTN, type 2 DM (last A1c reportedly 7.4), hyperlipidemia, remote nephrolithiasis.
PSH: appendectomy remote. No urologic surgery.
Home meds: tamsulosin 0.4 mg qHS, lisinopril 20 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg BID, atorvastatin 40 mg qHS, ASA 81 mg.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Social: lives with wife, retired machinist. Former smoker, quit ~15 yrs, 20 pack-yr. Occasional beer. No drugs.
FH: father MI age 70, mother DM.
ROS: positive fever, chills, dysuria, flank pain, weakness, poor intake. Negative for hematuria, vomiting, rash, neck stiffness.
ED COURSE:
Temperature 39.4 C at triage; WBC 21,300 with 14% bands.
Lactate 4.2 mmol/L at 02:10, 3.6 mmol/L repeat at 05:30.
Blood culture x2 and urine culture drawn at 02:20 before antibiotics.
Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g IV given at 02:45, 35 minutes after arrival; vancomycin added for coverage pending cultures.
Received 2.5 L normal saline bolus (30 mL/kg); BP after bolus 86/48, MAP 61.
Post-bolus vitals at 04:45: HR 118, BP 88/50, RR 26, T 38.9 C.
Norepinephrine started at 04:50 at 0.05 mcg/kg/min, titrated to 0.12 mcg/kg/min to keep MAP above 65.
Foley placed 03:10 for strict I/O, 60 mL concentrated urine returned initially.
PHYSICAL EXAM:
Gen: ill appearing, diaphoretic, rigors intermittently.
Vitals on transfer 05:55: T 38.7 C, HR 111, BP 97/62 on pressor, RR 24, SpO2 94% on 2 L NC.
HEENT: dry mucous membranes, no JVD, no scleral icterus.
CV: tachycardic, regular, no murmur, no rub. Extremities warm, cap refill 3 sec.
Pulm: tachypneic, clear to auscultation bilaterally, no crackles.
Abd: soft, mild suprapubic tenderness, right CVA tenderness. No rebound or guarding.
GU: prostate not examined acutely. Foley draining dark amber urine.
Neuro: arousable, oriented to person and place only, follows commands, no focal deficit, no meningismus.
Skin: no rash, no petechiae, no cellulitis.
LABS:
Urinalysis with large leukocyte esterase and more than 50 WBC per high power field; nitrite positive, many bacteria.
Creatinine 2.6 mg/dL (baseline 0.9 mg/dL); platelets 84,000.
Na 132, K 4.6, Cl 99, HCO3 17, BUN 38, glucose 214.
AST 34, ALT 29, T bili 1.4, alb 3.1, INR 1.3, fibrinogen 410.
ABG on 2 L: pH 7.31, pCO2 31, pO2 82, base deficit 8.
CXR: no consolidation, no effusion.
Renal US: no hydronephrosis, no stone visualized, prostate mildly enlarged.
ASSESSMENT:
61 yo M with septic shock, presumed urinary source, complicated by AKI, thrombocytopenia and lactic acidosis.
PLAN:
1. Sepsis/shock - ICU. Continue norepinephrine titrated to MAP >65. Repeat lactate q4h until clearing.
2. Source - complicated UTI/pyelonephritis. Continue pip-tazo and vancomycin. Follow blood and urine culture.
3. AKI - hold lisinopril, hold metformin. Trend creatinine and urine output q1h. Avoid nephrotoxins.
4. Thrombocytopenia - likely sepsis related. Daily CBC, monitor for bleeding.
5. Metabolic acidosis - resuscitation as above, recheck BMP at 10:00.
6. DM - hold metformin, SSI q4h, target glucose 140-180.
7. Resp - 2 L NC, wean for SpO2 >92%.
8. VTE ppx - hold pharmacologic given plt 84,000, SCDs for now.
9. NPO for now, IVF maintenance after resuscitation. Family updated at bedside with son.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 - ICU
lines: ICU PROGRESS NOTE - HD2 07:20
S: Pt more awake this AM, knows he is in hospital. Still feels weak, dysuria improved. Denies chest pain or dyspnea.
Overnight: norepinephrine requirement peaked at 0.12 mcg/kg/min around 05:00 HD1, now down to 0.04 mcg/kg/min.
Urine output 0.6 mL/kg/hr over last 6 hrs, up from 0.2 mL/kg/hr.
O: T max 38.4 C, T now 37.6 C. HR 96, BP 104/64 (MAP 77) on low dose pressor, RR 20, SpO2 95% on 2 L NC.
Exam: alert, oriented x3. Mucous membranes moist. Lungs clear. Abd soft, mild right CVA tenderness, less than yesterday.
Foley draining amber urine, 980 mL last 24h. No edema. No rash or petechiae.
Lactate 2.1 this AM, down from prior values.
Micro: blood culture x2 and urine culture pending, no growth reported yet at this hour.
A/P:
1. Septic shock, urinary source - improving. Wean norepinephrine as MAP allows, goal off today.
2. Continue piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g IV q6h and vancomycin per pharmacy dosing, trough as scheduled.
3. AKI - creatinine trending down to 2.2 from 2.6. Lisinopril and metformin remain held. Strict I/O.
4. Thrombocytopenia plt 79,000 - stable, no bleeding. Continue SCDs, no pharmacologic VTE ppx today.
5. Metabolic acidosis resolving, HCO3 20. Continue maintenance IVF at 100 mL/hr, reassess at noon.
6. DM - SSI, glucose 148-192 overnight, add correction at qHS.
7. Nutrition - advance to clear liquids, aspiration risk low.
8. Dispo - likely step-down HD3 if off pressor overnight. Wife updated 07:10.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD3 - Step-down
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD3 08:05
S: Pt feels much better. Ambulated to chair with RN. Appetite returning. No fever overnight, no dysuria.
Norepinephrine off at 14:30 HD2, no rebound hypotension. Transferred to step-down 20:00 HD2.
O: T max 37.4 C, T now 36.9 C. HR 84, BP 118/70, RR 16, SpO2 96% on room air.
Exam: alert and oriented x3, no distress. Lungs clear. Abd soft, nontender, no CVA tenderness. No edema.
I/O last 24h: in 2100 mL, out 2650 mL. Foley removed 07:30, voided 250 mL spontaneously at 07:55.
Labs: WBC 11,200, Hgb 11.4, plt 112,000. Creat 1.4, BUN 24, HCO3 23, K 4.0. Lactate 1.3.
Micro: blood culture positive for E. coli at 30 hours; urine culture growing gram negative rods, speciation pending.
Susceptibilities pending; organism reported pan-sensitive on preliminary panel.
A/P:
1. E. coli bacteremia with urinary source, septic shock resolved - off vasopressors >18 hrs, hemodynamically stable.
2. Antibiotics - remained on IV antibiotics through day 3. Vancomycin discontinued this AM given gram negative organism only.
3. Continue pip-tazo IV today; plan to narrow to oral agent per final susceptibilities with 7 day total course.
4. Repeat blood cultures drawn 08:00 to document clearance.
5. AKI - resolving, creatinine 1.4 from peak 2.6. Restart lisinopril once creat near baseline, not today.
6. Thrombocytopenia recovering, plt 112,000. Start subcutaneous heparin VTE ppx.
7. DM - restart metformin when creatinine at baseline; continue SSI, glucose 132-165.
8. Urology - no obstruction on imaging; outpatient follow up for BPH and recurrent UTI risk.
9. PT eval for deconditioning. Advance diet to regular.
10. Dispo - anticipate discharge home HD4 if afebrile and cultures clearing. Son updated by phone 08:40.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - E. coli Bacteremia/Urosepsis
lines: DISCHARGE SUMMARY - discharged HD4 14:20
Admitting diagnosis: sepsis, presumed urinary source.
Discharge diagnoses: E. coli bacteremia with acute pyelonephritis; septic shock, resolved; AKI, resolved; sepsis associated thrombocytopenia, resolved; BPH; type 2 DM; HTN.
HOSPITAL COURSE:
61 yo male presented at 02:10 HD1 with fever, dysuria, flank pain and confusion.
Temperature 39.4 C at triage; WBC 21,300 with 14% bands.
Lactate 4.2 mmol/L at 02:10, 3.6 mmol/L repeat at 05:30.
Urinalysis with large leukocyte esterase and more than 50 WBC per high power field; blood culture x2 and urine culture drawn at 02:20 before antibiotics.
Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g IV given at 02:45, 35 minutes after arrival; vancomycin added empirically.
Received 2.5 L normal saline bolus (30 mL/kg); BP after bolus 86/48, MAP 61.
Post-bolus vitals at 04:45: HR 118, BP 88/50, RR 26, T 38.9 C.
Norepinephrine started at 04:50 at 0.05 mcg/kg/min, titrated to 0.12 mcg/kg/min to keep MAP above 65. Weaned off 14:30 HD2.
Initial labs notable for creatinine 2.6 mg/dL (baseline 0.9 mg/dL); platelets 84,000.
Blood culture positive for E. coli at 30 hours; urine culture same organism, pan-sensitive.
Vancomycin stopped HD3. Pt remained on IV antibiotics through day 3, narrowed to oral cephalexin HD4 per susceptibilities.
Repeat blood cultures from HD3 no growth to date.
Creatinine improved to 1.1 on HD4; platelets 148,000. WBC 8,900, afebrile >36 hrs.
Renal US without hydronephrosis or obstructing stone.
DISCHARGE EXAM: T 36.8, HR 78, BP 122/74, RR 16, SpO2 97% RA. Alert, abd soft nontender, ambulating independently.
DISCHARGE MEDS:
Cephalexin 500 mg PO q6h to complete total 7 day antibiotic course.
Resume lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg qHS, tamsulosin 0.4 mg qHS, ASA 81 mg.
Metformin 1000 mg BID resumed at discharge given creatinine near baseline.
Acetaminophen 650 mg q6h prn.
INSTRUCTIONS:
Drink 2 L fluids daily unless told otherwise. Complete full antibiotic course.
Return for fever above 38.0 C, shaking chills, flank pain, vomiting, inability to urinate, or lightheadedness.
No heavy lifting or driving until cleared; expect fatigue for 1-2 weeks.
FOLLOW UP:
Primary care in 5-7 days for repeat BMP and CBC.
Urology in 3-4 weeks to evaluate BPH and recurrent UTI risk.
Discharged home with wife, discharge instructions reviewed with pt and wife, both verbalized understanding.
Condition at discharge: stable, improved.
